parts.latex:
The formula below is used to calculate an estimate for the blood alcohol content (BAC) of males.

$$\text{BAC}_{male}=\dfrac{10N-7.5H}{6.8M}$$

where $N$ is the number of standard drinks consumed, $H$ is the number of hours between the first and the last drink, and $M$ is the mass in kilograms.

Stephen weighs 98 kilograms. He consumed 6.5 standard drinks between 6:00 pm and 9:45 pm. He then stopped drinking alcohol.

His BAC reached zero at 1:15am. Calculate the rate at which his body metabolised the alcohol, in terms of BAC per hour. Give your answer correct to four decimal places.

dif.r: Find times, BAC from formula, then deduce rate unaided

solutions.latex:
Stephen drank from 6:00 pm to 9:45 pm, so $H=3.75$ hours.

Substitute into the formula with $N=6.5$ and $M=98$.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{BAC}&=\dfrac{10\times 6.5-7.5\times 3.75}{6.8\times 98}\\&=0.0553346\ldots\end{aligned}$$
His BAC reached zero 3.5 hours after 9:45 pm (at 1:15 am).
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Rate of metabolism}&=\dfrac{\text{BAC}}{\text{time taken}}\\&=\dfrac{0.0553346\ldots}{3.5}\\&\approx 0.0158 \text{ BAC/hour (to 4 d.p.)}\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Expresses the time spent drinking as a decimal, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
Gordon rated eleven restaurants out of 10. His ratings are listed below.

$$3,\ 3,\ 4,\ 4,\ 4,\ 5,\ 7,\ 7,\ 8,\ 9,\ 9$$

Gordon visited a new restaurant and rated it, adding the rating to the list above. The new rating did not affect the median, but did lower the mean.

Find the rating Gordon gave the new restaurant.

dif.r: Reason how added value affects even-count median and mean

solutions.latex:
The current median is $5$ and the current mean is $5.72$.

For the median to stay unchanged, the new rating must be $5$.

This also lowers the mean, since $5<5.72$.
$$\therefore \text{the new rating is } 5$$

dif.r: Angle sum then standard sine rule for side

figures.cap: triangle PQR

solutions.latex:
The angle sum of a triangle is $180^\circ$.
$$\angle PRQ=180^\circ-(51^\circ+46^\circ)=83^\circ$$
By the sine rule:
$$\begin{aligned}\dfrac{x}{\sin 83^\circ}&=\dfrac{10}{\sin 51^\circ}\\x&=\dfrac{10\times\sin 83^\circ}{\sin 51^\circ}\\&\approx 12.77 \text{ cm (to 2 d.p.)}\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Uses the sine rule, or equivalent merit

questions.stem: Buns & Roses sells bread rolls for \$0.80 each. The cost, $C$ dollars, of making $n$ bread rolls is given by the equation $C=300+0.2n$.

parts.label: a
parts.latex: How much does every 100 bread rolls made add to the cost of production?

dif.r: Read per-unit cost from linear equation, multiply by 100

parts.label: b

dif.r: Graph two lines and read break-even intersection

parts.label: c
parts.latex: How many bread rolls must be sold to make a profit of \$240?

dif.r: Form profit equation from income and cost, solve linear

figures.cap: blank grid for cost and income graphs
solution sketch: cost and income lines drawn on the grid, meeting at (500, 400)

solutions.latex:
Each roll adds $\$0.20$ to the cost.
$$100\times 0.2=\$20$$

\exfigure{850_q24_s1}

The graphs intersect at $n=500$, so 500 bread rolls must be sold to break even.
criteria: Draws the graph, OR finds the value of $n$ required to break even

solutions.latex:
Profit is income minus cost.
$$\begin{aligned}240&=0.8n-(300+0.2n)\\240&=0.6n-300\\0.6n&=540\\n&=900\end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore 900 \text{ bread rolls must be sold}$$
criteria: Uses the difference between income and cost, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
Aisha used her credit card to buy 1500 shares at a price of \$7.50 per share. A brokerage fee of $1.2\%$ was also charged on the purchase.

At the end of her first year owning the shares, she collected an annual dividend at a yield of $5.5\%$. She then used this dividend to pay back part of her credit card debt.

Calculate the amount Aisha still owes on her credit card given that the interest rate on the credit card is $20\%$ per annum, compounded daily.

dif.r: Combines brokerage, daily compounding debt and dividend yield in unguided sequence

solutions.latex:
The cost of the shares includes the $1.2\%$ brokerage fee.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Cost of buying shares}&=1500\times 7.50\times 1.012\\&=\$11\,385\end{aligned}$$
The debt grows for one year at $20\%$ per annum, compounded daily.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Amount owing after one year}&=11\,385\left(1+\dfrac{20\%}{365}\right)^{365}\\&=\$13\,904.91\end{aligned}$$
The dividend is $5.5\%$ of the value of the shares.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Dividend}&=5.5\%\times 1500\times 7.50\\&=\$618.75\end{aligned}$$
The dividend is then paid off the debt.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Amount owing after repayment}&=13\,904.91-618.75\\&=\$13\,286.16\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds the dividend paid, or equivalent merit
Finds the amount owing after one year before a repayment is made, or equivalent merit
Finds the cost of purchasing the shares, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
Kim develops a fashion application worth \$40 000. Due to advancements in technology, the app depreciates by $22\%$ each year. She then sells the app after using it for 5 years.

Calculate the price at which Kim sells her app.

dif.r: Direct substitution into declining-balance formula

solutions.latex:
Using the depreciation formula $S=V_0(1-r)^n$:
$$\begin{aligned}S&=40\,000\left(1-\dfrac{22}{100}\right)^5\\&=\$11\,548.70\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Uses the depreciation formula, or equivalent merit

questions.stem:
The operating loss, $L$ millions of dollars, of mining black opals in Lightning Ridge, varies inversely with the amount of opals mined, $M$ kilograms, according to the equation

$$L=\dfrac{k}{M}$$

The Lightning Ridge Mining Company lost 36 million dollars mining 3 kilograms of black opals.

parts.label: a
parts.latex: Find the value of $k$.

dif.r: Single substitution into given inverse variation equation

parts.label: b
parts.latex: What is the operating loss when 9.5 kilograms of black opals are mined, correct to three significant figures?

dif.r: Substitute into found equation and round to 3 s.f.

solutions.latex:
Substitute $L=36$ and $M=3$ into $L=\dfrac{k}{M}$.
$$\begin{aligned}36&=\dfrac{k}{3}\\ \therefore k&=108\end{aligned}$$

Substitute $k=108$ and $M=9.5$.
$$\begin{aligned}L&=\dfrac{108}{9.5}\\&=11.4\text{ million dollars}\quad\text{(correct to 3 significant figures)}\end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ L\approx \$11.4 \text{ million}$$
criteria: Uses their value of $k$ from part (a), or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
Roger’s flight itinerary is shown below. It details the departure and arrival times of the flights on his journey from Sydney to London. Only local times are shown in the table, and all departures and arrivals occur on the same Sunday.

\exfigure{850_q28_1}

Roger knows that Sydney is 7 hours ahead of Dubai, and that Dubai is 3 hours ahead of London.

How long did Roger spend flying?

dif.r: Two flight legs, each needing time-zone conversion, then summing durations

figures.cap: flight itinerary table

solutions.latex:
Sydney is 7 hours ahead of Dubai, so when the flight leaves Sydney it is 23:00 on Saturday in Dubai.

Landing at 13:20 on Sunday means the first flight took 14 hours 20 minutes.

Dubai is 3 hours ahead of London, so when the flight leaves Dubai it is 13:05 on Sunday in London.

Landing at 20:00 on Sunday means the second flight took 6 hours 55 minutes.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Total flight time}&=14\text{ hr }20\text{ min}+6\text{ hr }55\text{ min}\\&=21\text{ hr }15\text{ min}\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds the flight time of ONE of the flights, or equivalent merit
Finds the time AND day in Dubai when Roger departs Sydney, or equivalent merit
Finds the time in Dubai when Roger departs Sydney, or equivalent merit

parts.label: a
parts.latex: How much interest does Thai pay in the first month?

dif.r: Monthly rate applied to principal; one standard step

parts.label: b
parts.latex: How much interest does Thai pay in total over the life of the loan? Give your answer to the nearest cent.

dif.r: Read PV factor, find repayment, total repaid, subtract principal

figures.cap: present value factors for an annuity of $1

solutions.latex:
Interest for one month uses the simple interest formula with the monthly rate.
$$\begin{aligned}I&=250\,000\times\dfrac{8.4\%}{12}\times 1\\&=\$1750\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Uses the simple interest formula, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
The monthly rate and number of periods are:
$$r=\dfrac{8.4\%}{12}=0.7\%\text{ per month}$$
$$n=12\times 5=60\text{ months}$$
From the table, the present value factor for $r=0.7\%$, $n=60$ is $48.85587$. The repayment is the loan divided by this factor.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Monthly repayment}&=250\,000\div 48.85587\\&=\$5117.0924\\&\approx\$5117.09\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Total repaid}&=60\times 5117.09\\&=\$307\,025.40\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Interest paid}&=307\,025.40-250\,000\\&=\$57\,025.40\quad\text{(to the nearest cent)}\end{aligned}$$
Alternate solution:
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Interest paid}&=(250\,000\div 48.85587)\times 60-250\,000\\&=\$57\,025.54\quad\text{(to the nearest cent)}\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds the value of the monthly repayment, or equivalent merit
Finds the present value factor, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Source gives two answers ($57 025.40 and $57 025.54) from rounding the repayment at different stages; both kept as in the guideline.

questions.stem: A cylindrical tank is used to store pesticide for use at a park. The tank measures 6 metres in height and has a diameter of 3 metres.

parts.label: a
parts.latex: Find the volume of pesticide that can be stored in the tank, correct to two decimal places.

dif.r: Cylinder volume formula with radius from diameter

parts.label: b

dif.r: Standard two applications of the trapezoidal rule from diagram

parts.label: c
parts.latex:
The pesticide is to be evenly spread across the park.

Find the amount of pesticide, in litres, that is required for each square metre of land, correct to two decimal places.

dif.r: Convert cubic metres to litres and divide by area

figures.cap: aerial view of the park with offsets 190 m, 152 m, 0 over 250 m

solutions.latex:
The tank is a cylinder with radius $r=\dfrac{3}{2}=1.5$ m, so use $V=\pi r^2 h$.
$$\begin{aligned}V&=\pi r^2h\\&=\pi\times 1.5^2\times 6\\&=42.411508\ldots\\&\approx 42.41\text{ m}^3\quad\text{(correct to 2 d.p.)}\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds the radius of the cylinder, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
There are two trapezoids, each of height $125$ m, using the parallel sides shown in the diagram.
$$A\approx\dfrac{125}{2}(190+152)+\dfrac{125}{2}(152+0)$$
$$\therefore A\approx 30\,875\text{ m}^2$$
criteria: Finds the height of each trapezium, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Since $1\text{ m}^3=1000$ L:
$$\text{volume of pesticide}=42.4115008\text{ m}^3=42\,411.5008\text{ L}$$
$$\begin{aligned}\text{pesticide per m}^2&=\dfrac{42\,411.5008\text{ L}}{30\,875\text{ m}^2}\\&\approx 1.37\text{ L/m}^2\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds the volume of pesticide in litres, or equivalent merit

questions.stem:
The population of rabbits in a town is estimated to be 1000 in the year 2000. The population increases by $80\%$ each year. The population of the rabbits after $n$ years is given by

$$P=a^n\times 1000$$

where $P$ is the population of the rabbits and $a$ is a constant.

parts.label: a
parts.latex: Find the population of rabbits in the year 2009, correct to three significant figures.

dif.r: Identify growth factor 1.8 and n=9, then evaluate

parts.label: b
parts.latex:
At the end of the year 2009, a disease enters the rabbits’ ecosystem, decreasing the population by $80\%$ each year.

During which year will the rabbit population return to its initial population of 1000?

dif.r: Build new decay model from 2009 value; trial values to find year

solutions.latex:
The year 2009 is $n=9$ years after 2000, and $a=1.8$ for an $80\%$ increase.
$$\begin{aligned}P&=1.8^9\times 1000\\&\approx 198\,000\text{ rabbits}\quad\text{(3 sig. fig.)}\end{aligned}$$

A decrease of $80\%$ each year means multiplying by $0.2$. The population $n$ years after 2009 is
$$P=0.2^n\times 198\,000$$
Try values of $n$:
$$\begin{aligned}n=3:&\quad P=1584\\n=4:&\quad P=316.8\end{aligned}$$
The population falls below 1000 in the 4th year after 2009.
$$\therefore\text{ the year 2013}$$
criteria: Uses an appropriate method to find $n$, for example trial and error

questions.stem: At a local fast food restaurant, the probability, $W$, of the ice cream machine working on any given day is $40\%$. Ronald visits the restaurant on three consecutive days attempting to order an ice cream.

parts.label: a

dif.r: Three-stage tree and at-least-one via complement

parts.label: b
parts.latex: Find the probability that Ronald only successfully orders an ice cream on one out of three visits to the restaurant.

dif.r: Counts three arrangements of exactly one success across three stages

figures.cap: partially completed three-stage probability tree
solution sketch: completed tree diagram

criteria: Finds the probability of the ice cream machine working on all three days, or equivalent merit
Completes the tree diagram, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
There are three orders in which the machine works on exactly one day, each with the same probability.
$$\begin{aligned}P(W\text{ on one day only})&=P(W\overline{W}\,\overline{W})+P(\overline{W}W\overline{W})+P(\overline{W}\,\overline{W}W)\\&=3\times 0.4\times 0.6\times 0.6\\&=0.432\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds the probability of one of the three possible outcomes, or equivalent merit

questions.stem: Louie is a real estate agent earning a retainer of \$600 per week.

parts.label: a
parts.latex: Find Louie’s monthly retainer.

dif.r: Weekly to monthly via 52/12; common four-weeks trap

parts.label: b
parts.latex:
Every month Louie also earns a commission at a rate of $R\%$ on the first \$500 000 of his sales, and then at half of that rate on any sales above \$500 000.

Louie’s monthly income after selling \$750 000 worth of property is \$17 600.

Find the value of $R$.

dif.r: Set up equation for unknown tiered commission rate including retainer

solutions.latex:
There are 52 weeks in a year and 12 months.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{monthly retainer}&=(600\times 52)\div 12\\&=\$2600\end{aligned}$$

Commission is $R\%$ on the first \$500 000 and $\dfrac{R}{2}\%$ on the remaining \$250 000. Add the retainer of \$2600 to equal \$17 600.
$$\begin{aligned}\left(\dfrac{R}{100}\times 500\,000\right)+\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\times\dfrac{R}{100}\times 250\,000\right)+2600&=17\,600\\5000R+1250R&=15\,000\\6250R&=15\,000\end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore R=2.4$$
criteria: Forms a valid equation to calculate the rate of commission

parts.label: a
parts.latex: The correlation coefficient is $0.8721$. Describe the association between weekly income and life expectancy.

dif.r: Describe strength and direction from given correlation coefficient

parts.label: b
parts.latex: Find the value of $b$, correct to three decimal places.

dif.r: Read a point on line from graph, substitute to find intercept

skills: Line of best fit by eye

parts.label: c
parts.latex: Using the line of best fit, predict the life expectancy of a person with a weekly income of \$1000. Comment on the reliability of this prediction.

dif.r: Substitute then judge reliability as extrapolation

figures.cap: scatterplot of life expectancy against weekly income with line of best fit

solutions.latex:
The correlation coefficient $0.8721$ is close to $1$.

There is a strong positive linear correlation between weekly income and life expectancy.

The data point $(660, 76)$ lies on the line of best fit, so substitute it into $y=0.1072x+b$.
$$\begin{aligned}76&=0.1072\times 660+b\\ \therefore b&=5.248\end{aligned}$$

Substitute $x=1000$.
$$\begin{aligned}y&=0.1072\times 1000+5.248\\&\approx 112.45\quad\text{(to 2 d.p.)}\end{aligned}$$
This prediction is unreliable because it is an extrapolation of the data, since the independent variable in the original scatterplot only goes up to \$760.
criteria: Makes a valid prediction OR comments on the reliability of the prediction

questions.stem:
A warehouse has five main areas, represented by the vertices $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$ and $E$. The numbers on the edges represent the maximum number of forklifts per minute that can pass between each area. The path $BD$ allows $x$ number of forklifts through per minute.

\exfigure{850_q35_1}

parts.label: a
parts.latex: If the maximum flow of forklifts through the warehouse is 23 per minute, find the value of $x$.

dif.r: Identify minimum cut containing unknown and apply max-flow min-cut

parts.label: b
parts.latex:
For the warehouse to be profitable, the maximum flow of forklifts through the warehouse needs to be increased to 30 per minute. The warehouse staff can increase the flow along two edges of the network.

Provide two edges whose flow can be increased, and by how much, in order to increase the flow capacity to 30 forklifts per minute.

dif.r: Must reason about all cuts to choose two edge increases

figures.cap: flow network with Entry, A-E and Exit
solution sketch: network with minimum cut drawn, C = 20 + x

criteria: Gives evidence of cuts used to determine the maximum flow through the network diagram

solutions.latex:
Two cuts are below $30$ (with $x=3$):
$$\begin{aligned} A\to D,\ B\to D,\ B\to\text{Exit},\ E\to\text{Exit}: &\quad 7+3+8+5=23 \\ \text{Entry}\to A,\ \text{Entry}\to B,\ E\to B,\ E\to\text{Exit}: &\quad 11+10+3+5=29 \end{aligned}$$
$E\to\text{Exit}$ is on both, so increase it by $5$: the cuts become $28$ and $34$.
Then increase $A\to D$ by $2$ (or $B\to D$, or $B\to\text{Exit}$, by $2$): the first cut becomes $30$, and every other cut is at least $30$.
$$\therefore\ E\to\text{Exit}\ +5 \text{ and } A\to D\ +2$$
(Increasing $B\to\text{Exit}$ by $5$ instead, as the school's key does, leaves the second cut at $29$; $B\to\text{Exit}\ +5$ with $E\to\text{Exit}\ +2$ also works.)

meta.corrected: Corrected from source: the key said $B\to$Exit must go up by $5$; that leaves the cut around Entry, $C$, $E$ at $29$; $E\to$Exit $+5$ with $A\to D$ $+2$ reaches $30$.

parts.label: a
parts.latex: What are the values of $X$ and $Y$?

dif.r: Complete spreadsheet entries using monthly interest and balance

parts.label: b
parts.latex:
The account balance, $\$A_n$, at the end of $n$ months is given by the recurrence relation

$$A_n=(A_{n-1}+500)\times q$$

What is the value of $q$?

dif.r: Recognise multiplier as one plus monthly rate

parts.label: c
parts.latex: Find Sienna’s account balance at the end of the fifth month.

dif.r: Apply given recurrence relation twice

figures.cap: table of monthly balances and interest

solutions.latex:
The monthly interest rate is $\dfrac{4.2\%}{12}$, applied to the \$500 balance.
$$X=\dfrac{4.2\%}{12}\times 500=\$1.75$$
The new balance is the previous balance plus the deposit plus interest.
$$\begin{aligned}Y&=1005.26+500+5.27\\&=\$1510.53\end{aligned}$$

Each month the balance is multiplied by one plus the monthly rate.
$$\begin{aligned}q&=1+\dfrac{4.2\%}{12}\\&=1.0035\end{aligned}$$

criteria: Uses the answer from part (a) in the recursion formula, or equivalent merit

questions.stem:
Richie has inherited a large plot of land from a distant relative. The radial survey of the plot is shown below.

\exfigure{850_q37_1}

parts.label: a
parts.latex: Find the size of $\angle AOD$.

dif.r: Add two angles read from radial survey

parts.label: b
parts.latex: Find the area of triangle $AOB$, correct to the nearest square metre.

dif.r: Find included angle from bearings, apply area formula

skills: Area of a triangle (1/2 ab sin C)

parts.label: c
parts.latex: Richie stands at point $C$. Find the bearing of $O$ from where Richie is standing. Give your answer to the nearest degree.

dif.r: Cosine rule for angle, combine with bearing, then reverse bearing

figures.cap: radial survey of plot with points A, B, C, D around O

solutions.latex:
$\angle AOD$ is made up of $\angle DON$ and $\angle NOA$.
$$\begin{aligned}\angle AOD&=\angle DON+\angle NOA\\&=60^\circ+50^\circ\\&=110^\circ\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds the size of $\angle DON$, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
$$\angle AOB=140^\circ-50^\circ=90^\circ$$
Use the area formula with two sides and the included angle.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Area}&=\dfrac{1}{2}\times 305\times 230\times \sin 90^\circ\\&=35\,075\text{ m}^2\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds the size of $\angle AOB$, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Let $\angle COB=\theta$. Apply the cosine rule in triangle $COB$.
$$\begin{aligned}\cos\theta&=\dfrac{230^2+245^2-300^2}{2\times 230\times 245}\\ \theta&=\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{230^2+245^2-300^2}{2\times 230\times 245}\right)\\ \therefore\theta&\approx 78^\circ\quad\text{(to the nearest degree)}\end{aligned}$$
Hence the bearing of $C$ from $O$ is $140^\circ+78^\circ=218^\circ$.

The bearing of $O$ from $C$ is the reverse bearing, $218^\circ-180^\circ$.
$$\therefore\text{ the bearing of } O \text{ from } C \text{ is } 038^\circ$$
criteria: Finds the bearing of $C$ from $O$, or equivalent merit
Finds the size of $\angle COB$, or equivalent merit

parts.note: Normal probabilities from a z-table are not in the 2024 course; only the empirical rule is.

dif.r: Shift between distributions and symmetry to use table; non-routine setup

figures.cap: two normal curves, Group X mean 12 and Group Y mean 22, crossing at 17
table of cumulative probabilities for Group X
Group X normal curve shaded below n

solutions.latex:
The $Y$ distribution is the $X$ distribution shifted up by 10, so $P(Y\le 29)=P(X\le 19)$ and $P(Y\le 17)=P(X\le 7)$.
$$\begin{aligned}P(17\le Y\le 29)&=P(Y\le 29)-P(Y\le 17)\\&=P(X\le 19)-P(X\le 7)\\&=P(X\le 19)-P(X\ge 17)\quad\text{(symmetry about the mean 12)}\\&=P(X\le 19)-\big(1-P(X\le 17)\big)\\&=0.8275-(1-0.7500)\\&=0.5775\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds the equivalent probabilities in the distribution of $X$, or equivalent merit
Expresses the desired probability as a sum, or difference, of other probabilities in the distribution of $Y$, or equivalent merit

It is given that $A = \dfrac{h}{2}(a + b)$ and $h = 7$, $a = 9$ and $b = 11$.

What is the value of $A$?

dif.r: Direct substitution into a given formula

solutions.latex:
Substitute into the given formula.
$$\begin{aligned} A &= \dfrac{7}{2}(9 + 11) \\ &= 70 \end{aligned}$$
Hence the answer is A.

parts.latex:
An investment of \$$P$ earns interest at a rate of $r$ per annum compounded annually, where $r$ is a decimal, for $n$ years.

Which of the following expressions can be used to calculate the amount of interest earned on the investment?

dif.r: Choose compound interest expression: future value minus principal

solutions.latex:
The compound interest earned is the future value minus the present value.
$$\begin{aligned} I &= FV - PV \\ &= P \times (1 + r)^n - P \end{aligned}$$
Hence the answer is D.

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Area}_{\triangle AOB} &= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 85 \times 80 \times \sin(140^\circ - 45^\circ) \\ &\approx 3387 \text{ m}^2 \end{aligned}$$
Hence the answer is D.

$$h = 9.8t - 4.9t^2 .$$

What is the stone's height when $t = 1$?

solutions.latex:

$$\begin{aligned} h &= 9.8(1) - 4.9(1)^2 \\ &= 4.9 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$

A homeowner borrows \$155 000. Interest is charged on the balance owing at a rate of $0.6\%$ per month. A repayment of \$1200 is made at the end of each month.

What is the balance of the loan after the repayment at the end of the second month?

dif.r: Two iterations of reducing-balance loan calculation

solutions.latex:
Each month the balance is multiplied by $1.006$, then the repayment is subtracted.
$$V_0 = \$155\,000$$
$$V_1 = V_0 \times 1.006 - 1200 = \$154\,730$$
$$V_2 = V_1 \times 1.006 - 1200 = \$154\,458.38$$
Hence the answer is A.

parts.latex:
The gradient of the least-squares regression line is given by the formula

$$m = r \times \dfrac{s_y}{s_x} .$$

The least-squares regression line has a gradient of $m = 2$ for a dataset where $s_y = 6$ and $s_x = 3$.

Which of the following is the correct value for $r$?

dif.r: Substitute values and solve formula in reverse for r

solutions.latex:
Substitute $m = 2$, $s_y = 6$, $s_x = 3$ into the formula.
$$\begin{aligned} 2 &= r \times \dfrac{6}{3} \\ 2 &= 2r \\ r &= 1 \end{aligned}$$
Hence the answer is D.

parts.latex:
Blood alcohol for a female can be estimated using the following BAC formula

$$\text{BAC}_{\text{Female}} = \dfrac{10N - 7.5H}{5.5M} ,$$

where $N$ is the number of standard drinks consumed, $H$ is the number of hours since they started drinking and $M$ is the person's mass in kilograms.

Georgia weighs 58 kg and had a BAC of 0.08 after drinking for 2 hours.

How many standard drinks did she have, to the nearest whole number?

dif.r: BAC formula used in reverse to solve for N

solutions.latex:
Substitute $\text{BAC} = 0.08$, $H = 2$ and $M = 58$ into the formula.
$$\begin{aligned} 0.08 &= \dfrac{10N - 7.5(2)}{5.5(58)} \\ 0.08 &= \dfrac{10N - 15}{319} \\ 10N - 15 &= 25.52 \\ 10N &= 40.52 \\ N &= 4.052 \approx 4 \end{aligned}$$
Georgia had 4 standard drinks, so the answer is C.

parts.latex:
Jo owns a machine that is initially worth \$500 000 and which depreciates at a rate of $18\%$ per year using the declining balance method.

How much will it depreciate in the third year?

dif.r: Declining balance values for two years, then difference

solutions.latex:
Use the declining balance formula for the value after $n$ years.
$$\text{Value after 2 years} = 500\,000(1 - 0.18)^2 = \$336\,200$$
$$\text{Value after 3 years} = 500\,000(1 - 0.18)^3 = \$275\,684$$
So the depreciation in the third year is
$$\begin{aligned} 336\,200 - 275\,684 &= \$60\,516 \end{aligned}$$
Hence the answer is A.

parts.latex:
A measurement of 45 centimetres was found to have a percentage error of $\pm 0.11\%$.

Which of the following would best represent the absolute error?
parts.note: Percentage error and absolute error are not in the 2024 course.

dif.r: Percentage error formula used in reverse for absolute error

solutions.latex:
Use the percentage error formula.
$$\text{Percentage error} = \dfrac{\text{absolute error}}{\text{measurement}} \times 100\%$$
So
$$\begin{aligned} AE &= 0.11\% \times 45 \\ &= \pm 0.0495 \\ &\approx \pm 0.05 \text{ cm} \end{aligned}$$
Hence the answer is B.

meta.format_note: Source wrote the percentage error formula without the factor of 100%; it is included here and the working is unchanged.

dif.r: Recognise shared angle so sine cancels in area ratio

skills: Area of a triangle (1/2 ab sin C)

figures.cap: triangles ABC and ADE, not to scale

solutions.latex:
Both triangles share the angle $A$, so use the area formula with two sides and the included angle.
$$\text{Area}_{\triangle ABC} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 3 \times 4 \times \sin A = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 12 \times \sin A$$
$$\text{Area}_{\triangle ADE} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 7 \times 10 \times \sin A = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 70 \times \sin A$$
The ratio is
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{1}{2} \times 12 \times \sin A : \dfrac{1}{2} \times 70 \times \sin A &= 12 : 70 \\ &= 6 : 35 \end{aligned}$$
Hence the answer is C.

parts.latex:
A parent used Young's formula to calculate the required medication dosage for their child.

Young's formula is

$$\text{Dosage} = \dfrac{\text{Age of child (years)} \times \text{Adult dose}}{\text{Age of child (years)} + 12}.$$

They found that the child's dosage was one third of the adult dose.

How old is the child?

dif.r: Set up equation with unknown adult dose cancelling; solve rational equation

solutions.latex:
Let $a$ be the child's age in years and $d$ the adult dose. Young's formula gives the child's dose as one third of the adult dose:
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{1}{3}d &= \dfrac{ad}{a + 12} \\ \dfrac{a}{a + 12} &= \dfrac{1}{3} \\ 3a &= a + 12 \\ 2a &= 12 \\ a &= 6 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the child is 6 years old}$$
criteria: Creates a correct equation with the child's age as the only variable, or equivalent merit
Attempts to use Young's formula, or equivalent merit

Lachlan is at a lookout. He looks up and sees a white-bellied sea eagle.

The distance from Lachlan to the eagle is 153 metres and it is at an angle of elevation of $63^\circ$.

Lachlan looks down and sees the eagle's nest. The distance from Lachlan to the nest is 87 metres and it is at an angle of depression of $27^\circ$.

Calculate the distance of the eagle from its nest. Answer correct to the nearest metre.

dif.r: Must notice elevation plus depression angles give right angle

figures.cap: solution sketch: diagram of Lachlan, eagle and nest

solutions.latex:
\exfigure{1266_q22_s1}

The angles at Lachlan add to a right angle.
$$63^\circ + 27^\circ = 90^\circ$$
Hence the triangle is right angled, and by Pythagoras' theorem
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Distance} &= \sqrt{153^2 + 87^2} \\ &\approx 176 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds that the triangle is right angled, or equivalent merit

Find the total amount of tax and Medicare levy that James must pay.

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Taxable income} &= 65\,800 - 650 \\ &= \$65\,150 \end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Tax payable} &= 5092 + 0.325 \times (65\,150 - 45\,000) \\ &= \$11\,640.75 \end{aligned}$$

The Medicare levy is $2\%$ of taxable income.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Medicare levy} &= 2\% \times 65\,150 \\ &= \$1303 \end{aligned}$$
The total is the tax payable from part (a) plus the levy.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Total} &= 11\,640.75 + 1303 \\ &= \$12\,943.75 \end{aligned}$$

parts.latex:
Luke needs a twelve-month loan for \$8000. He has the following loan options:

\begin{itemize}
\item A payday lender at $0.92\%$ per week, interest compounded weekly.
\item A bank at $11.99\%$ p.a., interest compounded monthly.
\end{itemize}

He will repay the loan with a single lump sum at the end of the twelve months.

How much more will it cost him if he takes the loan from the payday lender rather than the bank?

dif.r: Two compound interest calculations with different periods, then difference

solutions.latex:
Payday lender: $0.92\%$ per week for 52 weeks.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Amount} &= 8000 \times 1.0092^{52} \\ &= \$12\,879.72 \end{aligned}$$
Bank: $\dfrac{11.99\%}{12}$ per month for 12 months.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Amount} &= 8000 \times \left(1 + \dfrac{0.1199}{12}\right)^{12} \\ &= \$9013.71 \end{aligned}$$
The extra cost is the difference.
$$\begin{aligned} 12\,879.72 - 9013.71 &= \$3866.01 \end{aligned}$$
Alternative solution: compare the interest paid.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Payday interest} &= 12\,879.72 - 8000 = \$4879.72 \\ \text{Bank interest} &= 9013.71 - 8000 = \$1013.71 \\ \text{Difference} &= 4879.72 - 1013.71 = \$3866.01 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the payday lender costs } \$3866.01 \text{ more}$$
criteria: Finds the future value of both loans, or equivalent merit
Finds the future value of one loan, or equivalent merit

parts.latex: Using four applications of the trapezoidal rule, estimate the area of the concrete wall.

dif.r: Four applications of trapezoidal rule; routine but several strips

parts.label: b
parts.latex:
The concrete wall will have a thickness of 28 m.

Calculate the volume of concrete required to build the wall, correct to the nearest cubic metre.

dif.r: Multiply previous area by thickness; one step

figures.cap: front view of concrete wall with heights 15, 25, 20, 26, 14 m over 48 m

solutions.latex:
Divide the wall into four sections of width 12 m, with areas $A_1, A_2, A_3, A_4$. Using the trapezoidal rule, $A = \dfrac{h}{2}(d_f + d_l)$.
$$\begin{aligned} A_1 &= \dfrac{12}{2} \times (15 + 25) = 240 \text{ m}^2 \\ A_2 &= \dfrac{12}{2} \times (25 + 20) = 270 \text{ m}^2 \\ A_3 &= \dfrac{12}{2} \times (20 + 26) = 276 \text{ m}^2 \\ A_4 &= \dfrac{12}{2} \times (26 + 14) = 240 \text{ m}^2 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Total area} &= 240 + 270 + 276 + 240 \\ &= 1026 \text{ m}^2 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Calculates the area of the wall with one error

solutions.latex:
The volume is the area of the wall times its thickness.
$$\begin{aligned} V &= 1026 \times 28 \\ &= 28\,728 \text{ m}^3 \end{aligned}$$

meta.marker_note: Consequential on answer to part (a).

questions.stem:
The time taken for a colony of ants to break up a sandwich and carry it away to the nest is inversely proportional to the number of ants performing the task.

If there are 20 ants, then it takes 42 minutes for the sandwich to be taken to the nest.

parts.label: a
parts.latex: Calculate how long it takes for 32 ants to carry the sandwich to the nest.

dif.r: Find inverse variation constant then substitute; standard

parts.label: b
parts.latex:
Another group of ants takes 1 hour and 10 minutes to carry the sandwich to the nest.

How many ants are in this group?

dif.r: Convert time to minutes, solve inverse variation for n

solutions.latex:
Time is inversely proportional to the number of ants, so with $t$ the time and $n$ the number of ants,
$$t = \dfrac{k}{n}$$
Substituting $t = 42$, $n = 20$:
$$\begin{aligned} 42 &= \dfrac{k}{20} \\ k &= 840 \end{aligned}$$
So $t = \dfrac{840}{n}$. When $n = 32$:
$$\begin{aligned} t &= \dfrac{840}{32} \\ &= 26.25 \text{ minutes} \\ &= 26 \text{ minutes } 15 \text{ seconds} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correctly calculates the constant of proportionality, or equivalent merit
Attempts to calculate the inverse proportionality, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
1 hour 10 minutes is $t = 70$ minutes.
$$\begin{aligned} 70 &= \dfrac{840}{n} \\ n &= \dfrac{840}{70} \\ &= 12 \text{ ants} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Converts time to minutes and substitutes, or equivalent merit

questions.stem:
Scientists perform two wildlife surveys six months apart to estimate the total koala population in a valley.

In the first survey they tagged 50 koalas and then released them back into the wild.

In the second survey six months later, they caught and checked 80 koalas. Of these 80 koalas 15 had tags.

parts.label: a
parts.latex: What is the estimate for the number of koalas in the valley?

dif.r: Standard capture-recapture proportion

parts.label: b
parts.latex:
The scientists then discovered that 3 of the koalas that had been tagged in the first survey had been moved to another location to help with a breeding program, so were not in the valley at the time of the second survey.

What is the better estimate for the number of koalas in the valley at the time of the second survey?

dif.r: Must reason that removed tagged koalas reduce effective tagged count

solutions.latex:
The proportion of tagged koalas is the same in the sample as in the whole population, so with $T$ the total population,
$$\dfrac{T}{50} = \dfrac{80}{15}$$
$$\begin{aligned} T &= 50 \times \dfrac{80}{15} \\ &= 266 \cdot \dot{6} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{there are approximately 267 koalas in the valley}$$
criteria: Applies ratio to capture-recapture calculations, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
This is the same as if only 47 koalas had been tagged initially.
$$\begin{aligned} T_{\text{new}} &= 47 \times \dfrac{80}{15} \\ &= 251 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{a better estimate is 251 koalas}$$
criteria: Applies ratio to capture-recapture calculations, or equivalent merit

parts.latex: If she chose to invest one lump sum at the start of the twelve months, instead of making the monthly deposits of \$500, how much would she have had to invest to get the same final amount?

dif.r: Present value of final amount using compound interest formula

figures.cap: savings spreadsheet months 1 to 3
spreadsheet rows for months 11 and 12 with unknowns A, B, C, D

solutions.latex:
The interest in the first month is $\$2.50$ on a balance of $\$500$.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Monthly rate} &= \dfrac{2.50}{500} \\ &= 0.5\% \text{ per month} \end{aligned}$$

$A$ and $B$ are the balance at the end of the month and the start of the next month.
$$\begin{aligned} A = B &= 5114.01 + 25.57 + 500 \\ &= \$5639.58 \end{aligned}$$
$C$ is the interest on $B$ at $0.5\%$.
$$\begin{aligned} C &= 0.005 \times 5639.58 \\ &= \$28.20 \end{aligned}$$
$D$ is the monthly deposit.
$$D = \$500.00$$
criteria: Calculates the interest, or equivalent merit
Finds the balance at the end of the month and the start of the following month, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Using the compound interest formula, the lump sum $PV$ grows to the final amount over 12 months at $0.5\%$ per month.
$$6167.78 = PV \times 1.005^{12}$$
$$\begin{aligned} PV &= 6167.78 \div 1.005^{12} \\ &= \$5809.46 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Applies compound interest formula, or equivalent merit

questions.stem:
Ten students were surveyed to find the correlation between the number of days they were absent from class while the topic was taught, $N$, and their result in Mathematics, $R$.

\exfigure{1266_q35_1}

parts.label: a
parts.latex:
Draw a scatterplot using the above table.

\exfigure{1266_q35_2}

dif.r: Plot given points on scatterplot

parts.label: b
parts.latex: Determine the equation of the least-squares line of best fit in the form $R = mN + c$, where $m$ and $c$ are correct to 1 decimal place.

dif.r: Calculator least-squares regression, write equation

parts.label: c
parts.latex:
Another student was surveyed, and their result in Mathematics was 70.

Using your answer from part (b), find the most likely number of days they were absent from class while the topic was taught.

dif.r: Substitute into regression line and solve for x, reversed use

figures.cap: table of absences N and results R
blank axes for scatterplot of R against N
solution sketch: scatterplot with line of best fit

solutions.latex: \exfigure{1266_q35_s1}

From the calculator, the intercept is $90.3$ and the gradient is $-5.1$.
$$\therefore\ R = -5.1N + 90.3$$
criteria: Finds the gradient or vertical intercept of the least-squares line, or gets them in the wrong order, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Substitute $R = 70$ into $R = -5.1N + 90.3$.
$$\begin{aligned} 70 &= -5.1N + 90.3 \\ -20.3 &= -5.1N \\ N &= 3.98 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the student most likely had 4 absences}$$
Alternative solution: graph the least-squares line, draw a horizontal line from $R = 70$ to the line, then a vertical line down to $N = 4$.
criteria: Substitutes $R = 70$ into their equation from part (b), or graphs the least-squares line, or equivalent merit

questions.stem:
There are two bags of lollies. One bag has three green frogs and two red frogs, while the second bag has four green frogs and five red frogs.

One bag is chosen at random, and two frogs are picked from the bag, without replacement.

parts.label: a
parts.latex:
Complete the below tree diagram below by writing probabilities in the boxes.

\exfigure{1266_q36_1}

dif.r: Fill tree with bag choice and without-replacement probabilities

parts.label: b
parts.latex: Calculate the probability of picking two red frogs.

dif.r: Three-stage tree, sum two branches, without replacement

parts.label: c
parts.latex: Calculate the probability of picking at least one green frog.

dif.r: Complement of previous result; short once (b) known

figures.cap: partly completed two-stage tree diagram for two bags
solution sketch: completed tree diagram

solutions.latex: \exfigure{1266_q36_s1}
criteria: Completes at least one pair of branches correctly, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Each bag is chosen with probability $\dfrac{1}{2}$; then two reds are drawn without replacement.
$$\begin{aligned} P(\text{two red}) &= \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{2}{5} \times \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{5}{9} \times \dfrac{4}{8} \\ &= \dfrac{17}{90} \\ &\approx 18.9\% \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Attempts to calculate the probability, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Use the complementary event.
$$\begin{aligned} P(\text{at least one green}) &= 1 - P(\text{two red}) \\ &= 1 - \dfrac{17}{90} \\ &= \dfrac{73}{90} \\ &\approx 81.1\% \end{aligned}$$

dif.r: Sine rule ambiguous case, obtuse adjustment, angle sum, minutes

figures.cap: triangle ABC with AB=6 cm, AC=10 cm, angle C = 20°41'

solutions.latex:
Applying the sine rule in triangle $ABC$:
$$\dfrac{\sin \angle ABC}{10} = \dfrac{\sin 20^\circ 41'}{6}$$
$$\sin \angle ABC = \dfrac{10 \sin 20^\circ 41'}{6}$$
The calculator gives $36^\circ 4'$, but $\angle ABC$ is obtuse, so
$$\begin{aligned} \angle ABC &= 180^\circ - 36^\circ 4' \\ &= 143^\circ 56' \end{aligned}$$
Using the angle sum of a triangle:
$$\begin{aligned} \angle BAC &= 180^\circ - 143^\circ 56' - 20^\circ 41' \\ &= 15^\circ 23' \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Attempts to find an angle in the triangle, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
A large farm shed has a flat rectangular roof which is 10 metres wide by 20 metres long. During a storm 15 mm of rain falls onto the roof in 10 minutes.

Rain that falls on the roof drains immediately into a cylindrical rainwater tank with a diameter of 4 metres.

\exfigure{1266_q38_1}

Calculate the average rate at which the water level in the tank changes during the storm. Answer in centimetres per minute to 1 decimal place.

dif.r: Model rain volume into tank, unit conversions, rate of rise

figures.cap: cylindrical tank, diameter 4 m, partly filled

solutions.latex:
The volume of rain is the roof area times the depth, $15 \text{ mm} = 0.015 \text{ m}$.
$$\begin{aligned} V &= 10 \times 20 \times 0.015 \\ &= 3 \text{ m}^3 \end{aligned}$$
The tank has radius $2$ m, so using $V = \pi r^2 h$:
$$\begin{aligned} 3 &= \pi \times 2^2 \times h \\ h &\approx 0.24 \text{ m (nearest centimetre)} \end{aligned}$$
The rate is the rise in level over the 10 minutes.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Rate} &= \dfrac{24}{10} \\ &= 2.4 \text{ cm/min} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds the change in height in the water tank during the storm, or equivalent merit
Substitutes into the formula for the volume of a cylinder, or equivalent merit
Correctly finds the volume of water, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
A project requires activities A to F to be completed. The activity chart shows the immediate prerequisites and duration for each activity.

\exfigure{1266_q39_1}

A new activity, $X$, is added to the project, and has $A$ as an immediate prerequisite. No other activity has $X$ as an immediate prerequisite.

By first drawing a network diagram showing all seven activities, find the maximum duration of $X$ if it does not increase the minimum time to complete the project.

dif.r: Draw network, find critical path, reason about new activity's float

skills: Critical path and minimum completion time

figures.cap: activity chart: prerequisites and durations for A to F
solution sketch: network diagram with X added, ESTs and LSTs

solutions.latex:
\exfigure{1266_q39_s1}

From the network diagram, the critical path of the original activities is $A, C, D, E$, with a minimum project time of 15 minutes.

$X$ has $A$ as its immediate prerequisite, so it cannot start until $A$ finishes, at 6 minutes. No activity depends on $X$, so draw an edge from $X$ to the End.

For the project time to stay at 15 minutes, $X$ must finish by 15 minutes, starting at 6 minutes.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Maximum duration} &= 15 - 6 \\ &= 9 \text{ minutes} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Adds $X$ at the correct place in the network diagram, or equivalent merit
Finds the minimum time for the project before $X$ is added, or equivalent merit
Attempts to create a network diagram, or equivalent merit
